subject: Accounting
title: The PCAOB's Role
description: A micro-lesson that makes The PCAOB's Role usable.

hook.text: Before 2002, nobody regulated the auditors. Then Enron happened and Congress created the PCAOB.

buildup.text: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board inspects audit firms and enforces standards.

discovery.text: PCAOB inspectors review audit working papers and issue findings when quality falls short.

twist.text: Before the PCAOB, the profession regulated itself—a system that clearly failed.

climax.text: External oversight added accountability that self-regulation could never provide.

punchline.text: Who watches the watchmen? Now someone actually does.

quiz.question: Why was the PCAOB created?
options: To provide external oversight of audit firms after Enron
To set tax rates for corporations

details.summary: The PCAOB—Public Company Accounting Oversight Board—was created by Sarbanes-Oxley to oversee the auditors of public companies. This topic explains how the PCAOB inspects audit firms, sets standards, and enforces quality in the post-Enron era.
details.whyItMatters: Before the PCAOB, the auditing profession was self-regulated—and that self-regulation failed spectacularly with Enron and WorldCom. The PCAOB provides independent oversight that protects investors.
takeaways: The PCAOB was created in 2002 as part of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act response to Enron
It inspects registered audit firms and issues reports on audit quality deficiencies
PCAOB enforcement actions can include fines, censure, and barring individuals from auditing

faq.question: What does the PCAOB do?
faq.answer: The PCAOB registers and inspects accounting firms that audit public companies, establishes auditing standards, investigates potential violations, and takes disciplinary action against firms and individuals that fail to meet professional standards.

faq.question: How does the PCAOB inspect audit firms?
faq.answer: PCAOB inspectors review selected audit engagements, examining workpapers, testing procedures, and evaluating quality controls. Large firms are inspected annually; smaller firms at least every three years. Inspection reports are made public.
